name: Data stored on the carrier and offline access (embedded data, control hashes, signed carrier payloads, multi-carrier products)
scope_note: Extends m09-identification-carriers.json; it does not repeat the identifier schemes, the SGTIN-96 bit layout, the NDEF URI prefix table, NTAG 424 DNA SUN or the resolver behaviour recorded there. Covers: data that travels in the carrier itself (GS1 Digital Link query-string data attributes, GS1 compressed Digital Link URIs including the 2025 'eh'/'ex' EPC forms, NDEF messages with several records, UHF RFID user memory and '+AIDC data' in the EPC bank as defined by the GS1 EPC Tag Data Standard 2.3, the ISO/IEC 20248 DigSig only as TDS encodes it via AI 8030); the optional offline basic data and control hash of the draft DPP standardisation request; signed 2D-code payload precedents (EU Digital COVID Certificate HCERT, ICAO visible digital seals, SMART Health Cards, BSI TR-03137 metadata); products with more than one carrier (linear plus 2D, QR plus NFC, label plus RFID); carrier placement and durability in EU law; and what an engine can and cannot verify offline from a sample artifact. Leaves out: passport payload data models, resolver conformance and online access control (other method files), print-quality grading, and the content of every EN, ISO, IEC, DIN and AFNOR document (bibliographic metadata only, rule 5). NFC Forum specifications (including the Signature RTD) were not opened. The Apple Core NFC page returned no body, so iOS behaviour is not recorded.
summary: In this family the carrier is not only a pointer: it also carries data that a reader can use without a network. Three placements exist. First, an optical code holds a URL plus extra content, either GS1 Digital Link data attributes in the query string (for example expiry date AI 17 or a digital signature AI 8030) or a whole signed and compressed payload, as in the EU Digital COVID Certificate (CBOR, COSE_Sign1, zlib, Base45, prefix 'HC1:') and in ICAO visible digital seals (binary header, TLV message zone, raw ECDSA signature, usually in a Data Matrix). Second, an NFC tag holds an NDEF message with several records, for example a URI record first (which phones use for dispatch) followed by a media-type record with embedded data, or a hybrid UHF/NFC tag that outputs a compressed GS1 Digital Link URI with the EPC binary string after an 'eh' or 'ex' marker. Third, a UHF RFID tag holds the EPC in bank 01, optionally followed by '+AIDC data', and further attributes in user memory (bank 11) behind a Data Storage Format Identifier, where TDS 2.3 also places an AI 8030 digital signature in a 352-bit Data Format 17 structure. The EU baseline is thin: ESPR requires a carrier linked to a persistent unique identifier and allows one or more carriers per delegated act, and the Batteries Regulation requires a visible, legible and indelible QR code with high contrast; neither binding text asks for offline data or a control hash. Only the 2024 draft standardisation request lists optional control data (a hash of the registered passport, a counterfeit-information link) and six optional cross-sectoral basic data elements for offline consultation, and asks for offline and online integrity verification. The only binding passport hash in EU law today is in the registry's proof of registration (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Arts 2(16) and 9), with no algorithm, canonical form or file format published. End to end, an issuer serialises the embedded data, signs or hashes it, encodes it into one or more carriers that must agree on the identifier, and a verifier decodes, parses, checks the signature against a pinned trust list, compares the embedded hash or attributes with the online passport when it is reachable, and checks cross-carrier consistency. A conformance engine can do all of this offline from sample artifacts (images, NDEF dumps, EPC hex) with pinned keys, but it cannot prove that the carrier is attached to the genuine product, that a static signed code was not copied, or that print and durability rules hold.

maturity.spec_status: Mixed. The GS1 parts are ratified open standards, but GS1 limits compressed Digital Link URIs to closed systems. The DCC HCERT specification is stable but archived since July 2023 after the EU regulation expired; its trust framework continues under the WHO Global Digital Health Certification Network. ICAO visible digital seals are in force in Doc 9303 (8th edition, Amendment 1 of 14 June 2024). The DPP-specific offline data and control hash exist only as optional items in a 2024 draft Commission text; the adopted request and the resulting EN 18220 and EN 18246 were not read (protected).

maturity.adoption_evidence: Signed carrier payloads have mass-scale precedent: the EU DCC (HCERT) ran from 1 July 2021 until the regulation expired on 30 June 2023, and the WHO took up the system on 1 July 2023 (new-ec-dcc-page); a dark-web study shows forged certificates that official apps accepted, which shows that issuer key compromise defeats offline checks (10.1145/3530877). ICAO visible digital seals are used on visas and emergency travel documents (new-icao-9303-p13). GS1 2D-in-retail guidance shows linear plus 2D dual marking is the current retail practice, with co-location tests (new-gs1-2d-retail-pos-1-1). For DPPs no deployment of embedded offline basic data or a control hash was located; literature shows QR and RFID as the common DPP carriers (10.1016/j.spc.2025.01.014) and prototypes comparing QR and NFC with DIDs (10.1108/ci-02-2025-0074). Compressed EPC Digital Link URIs for hybrid UHF/NFC tags are ratified but restricted to closed systems (new-gs1-dl-compression-epc-1-0-0).
maturity.regulatory_alignment: Binding law requires a carrier linked to a persistent unique product identifier, physically present on the product, packaging or accompanying documents (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1)(a)-(b)); each delegated act names one or more carriers, their layout and position (Art. 9(2)(b)-(c)) and the granularity (Art. 9(2)(d)); a digital copy of the carrier or identifier goes to dealers and marketplaces free of charge within five working days (Art. 10(3)). Batteries: from 18 February 2027 a QR code per Annex VI Part C, linking LMT, industrial above 2 kWh and EV batteries to the passport (Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 13(6)), printed or engraved visibly, legibly and indelibly, or on packaging and documents where that is not possible (Art. 13(7)); alternative smart labels by delegated act (Art. 13(8)); new markings after re-use, repurposing or remanufacturing (Art. 13(9)); Annex VI Part C asks only for high contrast and a size that common hand-held readers decode. No binding text asks for offline data, an embedded hash or a signed carrier payload. The draft standardisation request (new-m604-draft-sr-2024-02, Annex II Part B points 2.4-2.6, 2.10 and 7.1-7.2) is the only EU text that names them, as optional items. The registry proof of registration carries a passport-version hash (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Arts 2(16) and 9(2)(e)), which is the natural reference for a carrier control hash, but the algorithm and input are unpublished.

L01_unique_identifiers.mechanism: The embedded payload must name the same identifier as the carrier link. GS1 Digital Link: the primary key and qualifiers stay in the path (/01/{GTIN-14}/10/{lot}/21/{serial}); embedded data attributes go in the query string as AI=value pairs and must not repeat the path identity (URI Syntax 1.7.0, sec. 4.10). A compressed EPC Digital Link holds no visible identifier: https://{stem}/eh{lower-case hex EPC binary} or https://{stem}/ex{base64url EPC binary}; the identifier appears only after decoding with TDS (worked example https://example.com/eh30164596f40c0e5cbe991a83 = SGTIN-96, header 0x30, filter 0, partition 5, company prefix 9528765, item reference 012345, serial 123456789123 = (01)09528765123457(21)123456789123; this session recomputed the decode and the base64url form 'MBZFlvQMDly-mRqD' with the standard library and both match the standard). DCC: identity of the signed object is inside the CBOR (claim -260 key 1), not in a URL; the key identifier kid is the first 8 bytes of the SHA-256 of the signer certificate in DER. ICAO VDS: header carries issuing country (C40, 2 bytes), signer identifier (2-letter country + 2 alphanumerics) and certificate reference (5 hex characters in header version 3; length-prefixed in version 4); certificate reference 0...0 is reserved for tests. TDS user memory: the DigSig domain authority identifier equals the GS1 Party GLN (AI 417) of the accountable organisation.

L01_unique_identifiers.law_delta: Law requires only a persistent unique identifier reachable through the carrier (ESPR Art. 10(1)(a)); it says nothing about identifiers inside embedded payloads or their equality across encodings.

L02_data_carriers.mechanism: Optical: QR Code or Data Matrix with a GS1 Digital Link URI and query attributes, for example https://id.example/01/09528765123457/21/ABC?17=271231&8030={base64url DigSig up to 90 chars}; AI 17 format N2+N6 YYMMDD and validAsDataAttribute true; AI 8030 'DIGSIG' format N4+Z..90, regex [0-9A-Za-z_-]{1,90}, requires a serialised key such as 01+21, 8006+21, 8010+8011, 8003, 8004, 8017, 8018, 00, 253 or 255 (AI JSON-LD 1.2). Extension (non-GS1) query keys must not be all-numeric; linkType and context are reserved (URI Syntax 4.10.1). Signed binary payload in QR: DCC chain JSON -> CBOR (CWT) -> COSE_Sign1 (CBOR tag 18) -> zlib (RFC 1950/1951) -> Base45 (RFC 9285) -> prefix 'HC1:' -> QR alphanumeric mode, error correction Q recommended, printed diagonal 35-60 mm. SMART Health Cards: compact JWS (ES256, header zip 'DEF', raw DEFLATE payload) -> 'shc:/' plus two decimal digits per character (ASCII minus 45) in QR numeric mode, up to QR version 22; multi-QR chunking 'shc:/2/3/' deprecated. ICAO VDS: magic 0xDC, version byte (0x02 = version 3, 0x03 = version 4), country, signer and certificate reference, issue date and signature date (3 bytes each, MMDDYYYY as integer), feature definition reference (1-254), document type category (odd values reserved for ICAO); message zone of tag|length|value features (tags 0-254, DER-TLV length 1-5 bytes, strings C40-encoded, upper case only); signature zone marker 0xFF; ISO-standardised 2D symbologies only (Data Matrix, Aztec, QR named); recommended module size at least 0.3386 mm on inkjet. NFC: one NDEF message, several records; header octet MB 0x80, ME 0x40, CF 0x20, SR 0x10 (payload length 1 byte when under 256 bytes, else 4 bytes), IL 0x08, TNF in the low 3 bits (0 empty, 1 well-known, 2 media type, 3 absolute URI, 4 external, 5 unknown, 6 unchanged; 7 rejected); media-type records carry an RFC 2046 type string (ndeflib checks the pattern [a-zA-Z0-9-]+/[a-zA-Z0-9-+.]+). Android uses only the first record for dispatch, so a DPP tag puts the URI record first and embedded data (for example an application/json or application/cbor record) after it; an Android Application Record should not be first; from Android 16 http(s) URI tags trigger ACTION_VIEW and from Android 17 need an explicit open-link action. For iOS background reading (iPhone XS and later), Apple's page says that the first URI record found is used and states no position requirement; with http(s) universal links or a fixed scheme list only (new-apple-corenfc-background), so a URI record at index 0 satisfies both platforms. Hybrid UHF/NFC tag: the NFC interface outputs a compressed EPC Digital Link URI ('eh'/'ex') and software decodes it. UHF RFID: EPC bank may hold '+AIDC data' after the EPC when the '+AIDC data toggle bit' (bit after the 8-bit header of the new schemes) is 1 (TDS sec. 14.5.1, 15.3); user memory bank 11 starts with an 8-bit DSFID: two MSBs Access Method ('10' Packed Objects per TDS Annex I-M, '00' No-Directory), one extension bit, five-bit Data Format ('01001' = GS1 Data Format 9 for AIs); DSFID 00010001 selects Access Method 17 for an AI 8030 DigSig: DAID 8 bits '11111110' + 44 bits PGLN, CID 16 bits, signature and timestamp 256+20 bits (one-year signing period at minute resolution), total 352 bits; the EPC is covered by the signature and including the TID is recommended for copy detection. The User Memory Indicator (Gen2v2) or Read User Memory indicator (Gen2v3) in the PC bits flags user memory content. Durability and placement: battery QR printed or engraved visibly, legibly, indelibly (Batteries Art. 13(7)); high contrast and readable size (Annex VI Part C).

L02_data_carriers.observable_black_box: From sample artifacts: the decoded text or bytes of each symbol, the symbology, the NDEF record list with TNF, type and payload, the EPC bank and user memory hex dumps, the payload size against carrier capacity. Not observable from a file: print contrast, module size on the physical item, indelibility, placement and tag read range.
L02_data_carriers.law_delta: Law fixes presence, visibility, legibility, indelibility and contrast only for battery QR codes and leaves carrier type to delegated acts; embedded data, multi-record layouts, RFID user memory and signed payloads are beyond law. The draft request asked standards to cover symbology, encoding, error correction, reference decoding, print and production quality and durability (new-m604-draft-sr-2024-02, Part B 2.2) and optional control and offline data (2.4-2.6).

L03_data_exchange_protocols.mechanism: Offline path: no protocol; the reader decodes the carrier locally. Online path where the carrier also holds a URL: a GS1 Digital Link carrier is followed by HTTP GET (resolver behaviour in m09); the whole query string, including embedded attributes, is passed on to the redirect target per the GS1 resolver standard as recorded in m09 (not re-read here). Compressed URIs: GS1 states that decompression happens in external software, that a compressed URI in an optical carrier counts as 'any URL', and that only applying the decompression algorithm and validating the result against the URI syntax shows whether a URL holds GS1 identifiers; GS1-conformant resolvers can decompress. The 'eh'/'ex' compression string is appended to a URI stem with no query or fragment and exactly one slash before it. Legacy compression (1.1.4) distinguishes partially compressed URIs (primary key uncompressed, final path segment compressed) from fully compressed ones by counting path components (primary key at odd position 3 from the right versus even positions in uncompressed URIs). Trust material for offline signature checks is fetched ahead of time: DCC trust list (CSCA and DSC lists aggregated by a Secretariat, daily download, 24-hour update target), SHC JWKS at {iss}/.well-known/jwks.json and CRL at /.well-known/crl/{kid}.json, ICAO signer certificate acquired out of band (it is not in the barcode).

L03_data_exchange_protocols.observable_black_box: Whether the embedded data are usable with no network; whether a resolver accepts and decompresses 'eh'/'ex' URIs (loopback test only); whether query attributes reach the redirect target.
L03_data_exchange_protocols.law_delta: None in law. The draft request names offline consultation when the reader is offline, the link is broken, the page is invalid or the server is down (new-m604-draft-sr-2024-02, Part B 2.5(a)-(d)).

L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.mechanism: Embedded carrier data has no API: it is written once at printing or tag encoding. Updates need a new label, a tag rewrite (if not locked) or, for batteries, new markings after re-use or remanufacturing (Batteries Art. 13(9)). Searchability stays with the online passport and the registry.
L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.observable_black_box: None beyond comparing embedded data with the online passport version.

L05_system_interoperability_data_models.mechanism: Embedded data needs a compact, self-describing model. GS1: AIs as keys with format strings and regexes from the AI JSON-LD (machine-readable oracle: formatString, regex, requires, excludes, validAsDataAttribute); in user memory, Packed Objects with an ID table registered as Data Format 9 (TDS Annex F, I-M). DCC: JSON schema (eu-dcc-schema, archived 2023-07-26) mapped to CBOR; test vectors compare decoded CBOR and JSON by decoding and re-encoding both sides because key order is not fixed. ICAO VDS: per document type a feature definition (tags, mandatory and optional features, length ranges); unknown tags may be present and must not affect validity if the signature verifies. NFC: media type of each record (RFC 2046) names the payload model. Draft DPP request lists six optional cross-sectoral basic data elements for offline use: passport owner (operator that created the passport), unique operator identifier (main manufacturer if different), facility identifier (main manufacturing stage), unique product identifier (as registered), an optional additional product identifier, and product group; no encoding is named.

L05_system_interoperability_data_models.law_delta: No binding model for embedded data. The six-element list is a draft, non-binding text; its numbering in the draft runs (2)-(7) with no item (1).

L06_storage_archiving_persistence.mechanism: The carrier is itself a persistent copy of the embedded data for the life of the label or tag; durability depends on the marking method (Batteries Art. 13(7) printed or engraved, indelible). The draft request motivates offline basic data as a fallback when the passport host is unreachable. Embedded data become stale when the online passport is updated; a control hash ties the carrier to one registered version only. Tag memory can be permalocked (TDS sec. 16.2.5 BlockPermaLock segment, not read in detail).
L06_storage_archiving_persistence.observable_black_box: Whether embedded data still match the current passport version; whether the embedded hash matches any registered version.
L06_storage_archiving_persistence.law_delta: Law gives no persistence role to embedded data; ESPR back-up copy rules concern hosted passports.

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.mechanism: Anything in a carrier is public to whoever reads it: query attributes, NDEF records, user memory (unless access-password protected at tag level) and signed payloads are readable without authentication; signing gives integrity, not confidentiality. The DCC places personal health data in the QR and relies on the holder controlling the paper; DPP offline data in the draft request are cross-sectoral basic elements, not restricted data. The draft request also asks the carrier to reference both public and restricted passport data (Part B 2.3, 2.9). Literature shows NDEF signature records can still be misused (signature not covering all records, or apps not enforcing it) (10.1109/nfc.2011.9, 10.1109/rfid-ta.2012.6404492).

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.observable_black_box: Whether a sample carrier embeds data that the declared access policy marks as restricted (leak check against the passport's restricted field list).
L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.law_delta: Law restricts access to some passport data (for example battery Annex XIII points 2-4 per m01); embedding such data in a carrier would bypass that, and no law text addresses it.

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.mechanism: Three integrity patterns. (1) Signed embedded payload: DCC COSE_Sign1 with alg ES256 (primary) or PS256 (RSASSA-PSS 2048, SHA-256), kid in protected (preferred) or unprotected header, verify signature before reading content, enforce exp (claim 4), check iat (claim 6) against the signer certificate validity, try every certificate whose truncated kid matches, check extended key usage OIDs against the certificate type; revocation by absence from the latest trust list, CRLs not assumed. ICAO VDS: signature over header plus message zone (excluding marker and length), ECDSA at least 256-bit with SHA-256 recommended, raw r||s each padded to key length, hash algorithm not encoded but deduced from the bit length of the curve order (SHA-224 up to 224, SHA-256 up to 256, and so on); algorithms per Doc 9303 Part 12. SHC: ES256 with P-256, kid = base64url SHA-256 JWK thumbprint, optional x5c chain whose SAN must match iss, revocation identifier rid (up to 24 base64url chars) and per-key CRL. GS1: AI 8030 DigSig in a Digital Link query or in user memory (TDS sec. 17; signature scheme defined in ISO/IEC 20248, bibliographic only). (2) Control hash: the draft request suggests a hash of the passport registered in the registry; the only binding hash is the registry's 'hash of a passport version' in the proof of registration, sealed with a qualified electronic seal and time-stamped (2026/1778 Arts 2(16), 9); no algorithm, canonicalisation or format is published, so a carrier hash cannot yet be compared deterministically with it. (3) Tag-bound authenticity: TID inclusion in the DigSig (TDS), public-key challenge-response tags with an NDEF tag authentication record (Saeed and Walter 2012) or SUN messages (m09). Limits: a valid signature on a static code proves origin of the data, not that the code is on the genuine item; copied QR codes and DigSigs verify everywhere; issuer key compromise lets forged payloads verify (dark-web DCC forgeries accepted by official apps, 10.1145/3530877).

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.observable_black_box: Offline from a sample with pinned trust material: signature valid or not, signer certificate chain and validity at the evaluation time, expiry, key usage, revocation against a pinned list snapshot, embedded hash equal or not to a hash of a declared passport version (once the hash input is declared). L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.law_delta: Adds integrity mechanisms that law does not require. Law has a sealed passport-version hash only in the registry's proof of registration (2026/1778 Art. 9), with the algorithm unspecified; the draft request asked standards for offline and online originality and integrity checks and 'electronically signed encoded data set' schemes (Part B 7.1).

L09_registry_and_customs.mechanism: The registry checks granularity and links item to batch and model identifiers (2026/1778 Art. 8) and issues a proof of registration with a passport-version hash (Art. 9). A carrier control hash in the draft request is defined as a hash of the passport registered in the registry, so the registry is the intended reference for offline integrity. No registry API for hash lookup was located.
L09_registry_and_customs.observable_black_box: With an operator-supplied proof of registration: whether its hash equals the hash embedded in the carrier (both opaque until an algorithm is declared).
L09_registry_and_customs.law_delta: Law does not link carriers to the registry hash; that link is only in the draft request.

L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.mechanism: Embedded data and hashes pin one passport version; every passport update makes a control hash stale unless the carrier is re-marked or the hash refers to an immutable first registration. Signed payloads carry their own validity window (DCC exp; VDS document issue and signature dates; SHC exp). Battery status changes need new markings that make the change reachable through the QR code (Batteries Art. 13(9)). DCC test-vector context carries a VALIDATIONCLOCK so expiry checks are deterministic. ICAO VDS lets signer certificates rotate through the certificate reference in the header; SHC asks issuers to rotate keys at least yearly.
L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.observable_black_box: Embedded version or hash against the passport version history; signature dates against the evaluation clock.
L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.law_delta: Law does not say which version a carrier hash should reference; the registry proof covers the latest version only and lasts 90 days (2026/1778 Art. 9).

L11_roles_and_governance.mechanism: Signed carriers need a trust framework: DCC used national CSCAs, DSC lists, an EU gateway and a Secretariat-aggregated trust list, now continued by the WHO network; ICAO uses CSCA-signed signer certificates exchanged bilaterally or via download (Appendix A workflow: signer certificate generation, seal generation, validation); SHC uses issuer JWKS plus optional directories; GS1 DigSig makes the GLN owner (PGLN, AI 417) the accountable domain authority. For DPPs no trust framework for carrier signatures exists in law; the ESPR implementing act on credentials is not located (m01). Compressed EPC Digital Link use needs a GS1 Policy B11 assessment and GSMP application standard before open supply chain use.
L11_roles_and_governance.observable_black_box: Whether the signer chains to the declared trust anchor in a pinned bundle; whether the declared trust framework exists.
L11_roles_and_governance.law_delta: No DPP trust framework for carrier-level signatures in binding law.

end_to_end_flows.name: Offline verification of a signed QR payload (HCERT-style profile applied to a DPP sample)
steps: 1. The issuer builds the embedded data as a CBOR claims map (identifier, issue time, expiry, data elements).
2. The issuer signs it as COSE_Sign1 (tag 18) with ES256 and a kid derived from the signer certificate.
3. The issuer compresses with zlib, encodes Base45, adds a context prefix and prints a QR code in alphanumeric mode.
4. The trust list operator publishes signer certificates; the verifier downloads a snapshot ahead of time.
5. Offline, the verifier decodes the QR, checks and strips the prefix, Base45-decodes, inflates, parses COSE.
6. The verifier finds certificates by kid, verifies the signature, checks validity, expiry and key usage at the evaluation time.
7. Only then the verifier parses the claims and compares the identifier with the carrier URL or the passport, when reachable.

end_to_end_flows.name: Hybrid UHF/NFC tag with compressed EPC Digital Link
steps: 1. The encoder writes an SGTIN (or SGTIN+ with +AIDC data) into the EPC bank.
2. The NFC interface exposes https://{stem}/eh{hex EPC} or /ex{base64url EPC} as an NDEF URI record.
3. A phone reads the URI and opens it; the resolver decodes the EPC with TDS or TDT and serves the uncompressed Digital Link context.
4. An offline app can decode the EPC itself and rebuild https://{stem}/01/{GTIN}/21/{serial}.
5. A UHF reader reads the same EPC over the air; both identifiers must be equal.

end_to_end_flows.name: Multi-record NFC tag with offline basic data
steps: 1. The encoder writes an NDEF message: record 1 well-known URI with the passport link; record 2 media-type record with offline basic data (for example the six draft elements); optional signature record.
2. A phone dispatches on record 1 and opens the link when online.
3. An offline app reads record 2 and displays the basic data.
4. A verifier checks that the identifier in record 2 equals the identifier in the URI and that any signature covers both records.

end_to_end_flows.name: Linear plus 2D dual-marked pack (retail transition)
steps: 1. The pack carries an EAN/UPC and a 2D code (GS1 DataMatrix or QR with Digital Link) with the same GTIN.
2. The 2D code sits within 50 mm of the linear code centre so a POS scanner can treat both as one item.
3. Attributes that appear in both symbols and in human-readable text match exactly.
4. The consumer scans the 2D code to reach the passport or other content.

end_to_end_flows.name: Control hash check against a registered passport version
steps: 1. The operator registers the passport; the registry can issue a sealed proof of registration with a passport-version hash.
2. The operator embeds a control hash in the carrier (draft request concept).
3. The verifier reads the hash offline; online, it fetches the passport, computes the hash with the declared algorithm and canonical form, and compares.
4. Today step 3 is not decidable: no algorithm, canonical form or file format is published.

failure_modes.fault: A multi-record NDEF message puts a media-type data record (or an Android Application Record) before the URI record. iOS may still find the link, because Apple's page states no position requirement for the URI record, but Android dispatches on record 1 and does not open the passport. The defect appears on one platform only.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Parse the NDEF dump from a sample and check that record index 0 has TNF 1 and type 'U' with an https URI (new-android-nfc-basics; new-apple-corenfc-background).

failure_modes.fault: The NFC URI record uses a custom URL scheme (for example an app scheme) instead of an https link, so iOS background reading ignores it and the phone shows no passport.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Check the scheme of the decoded URI record against https, from the sample artifact (new-apple-corenfc-background).

failure_modes.fault: The NFC tag of a product encodes a different serial than its printed QR code (tags encoded from a different batch file).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Cross-carrier equivalence over the declared sample set.

failure_modes.fault: A compressed 'eh' URI uses upper-case hex or carries a query string on the stem, so resolvers or apps fail to decompress.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Strict parse against Compression TS sec. 4.2.1.

failure_modes.fault: The embedded data record is placed first in the NDEF message, so phones do not open the passport link.
failure_modes.detectable_by: First-record check in the NDEF sample.

failure_modes.fault: Query attributes duplicate the path identity or use an AI not valid as a data attribute (for example AI 21 in the query).
failure_modes.detectable_by: AI JSON-LD validAsDataAttribute and path/query overlap check.

failure_modes.fault: Payload too large for the chosen symbol version, forcing low error correction or tiny modules that fail in the field.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Decoded symbol version and error-correction level from the sample (where the decoder exposes them); otherwise manual review.

failure_modes.fault: Extra application data written after the EPC in the EPC bank without the +AIDC toggle bit.
failure_modes.detectable_by: TDS 18.1.2 check on the EPC bank dump.

failure_modes.fault: Verifier reads the payload before verifying the signature, or accepts an unprotected kid that conflicts with the protected one.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Tampered vectors whose content is valid but whose signature fails must give fail, not partial pass.

failure_modes.fault: Truncated kid collision: verifier tries only the first matching certificate and rejects a valid payload.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Fixture with two certificates sharing the 8-byte kid.

failure_modes.fault: VDS signature stored DER-encoded instead of raw r||s, or r/s not left-padded to key length.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Length check of the signature zone against the key length.

failure_modes.fault: A static signed QR or DigSig copied onto a counterfeit product verifies as valid.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Not detectable from data alone; the report must state the limit. TID-bound signatures or dynamic tags reduce it.

failure_modes.fault: Issuer key leak or rogue issuance produces forged payloads that verify (as observed for DCC).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Only through trust-list revocation in the pinned snapshot; offline checks cannot detect it otherwise.

failure_modes.fault: Control hash computed over a non-canonical serialisation, so it never matches the registry hash.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Recompute with the declared canonical form; report mismatch with the computed value.

failure_modes.fault: Passport updated after printing; carrier hash or offline basic data now stale and contradict the online passport.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare embedded data with the current version and the version history.

failure_modes.fault: Restricted data (for example dismantling or test results) embedded in a public NFC record.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Carrier leak check against the declared restricted field list.

sources.what_it_shows: iOS background tag reading needs an NDEF URI record (TNF well-known, type 'U'). The system takes the first such record found and does not require it at index 0. Allowed URIs are universal links or a fixed list of schemes: http(s), mailto, sms, tel, facetime, facetime-audio, Apple Maps links and X-HM HomeKit setup codes. Custom schemes are not supported. The device must be iPhone XS or later. Background reading is blocked before the first unlock, during a Core NFC session, while Wallet or the camera is in use, and in airplane mode. The app receives the whole NDEF message as an NSUserActivity of type browsing-web.
